Two challenges with the lifetime testing setups were encountered: The delivery of the Fluxim system to MIT has been delayed due to the supply-chain issues, delaying our study of lifetime measurements with combined atmosphere and temperature control. Also, when utilizing the open source μSMU boards we obtained for our design of inexpensive lifetime measurement setups, we discovered multiple hardware and software issues in the public designs that we accessed. We are presently working with the developer of the board to address the unexpected hardware and software bugs. A further set of samples is measured through our low-cost lab built Keithley/LabView system (again as shown in Figs. 6.2 and 6.3). Samples are separated into two groups (each containing three devices) and stored under different environments. The first group is stored under room temperature (25oC) with a 44 % relative humidity. The second group is stored in an oven that is heated to 60oC with 20% relative humidity. Photovoltaic response measurement on all samples is then carried out. We compare the Structural Similarity Index Measurement (SSIM) by calculating the L1 norm and L2 norm for each pair of measured curves, followed by the calculation of the absolute average to get the final percent variation between different device measurements.
